btsp_parameters.name: plateau_share
btsp_parameters.why: share of CA1 cells that get a plateau for each drawing (f_q in Wu and Maass 2025, measured near 0.005); chosen on background-alphabet drawings

btsp_parameters.name: ec3_baseline
btsp_parameters.why: a yes-or-no choice: plateau drive measured against each cell's drive from the mean background-alphabet EC code (yes) or raw (no); chosen on background-alphabet drawings

btsp_parameters.name: connect
btsp_parameters.why: probability that a CA3 cell synapses on a CA1 cell, 0.6 (f_w in Wu and Maass 2025, from about 15,000 inputs of 25,000)

btsp_parameters.name: gate
btsp_parameters.why: probability 0.5 that an eligible synapse changes (Wu and Maass 2025, Eq. 1: half the 10 s window gives LTP, half LTD)

btsp_parameters.name: initial_weight
btsp_parameters.why: every CA3-to-CA1 weight starts at 0 (Wu and Maass 2025, Methods)

btsp_parameters.name: ca1_units
btsp_parameters.why: CA1 cells per CA3 cell, the human ratio 16M/1.7M or the rat ratio 350k/210k

btsp_parameters.name: window
btsp_parameters.why: each plateau's seconds-long window covers one drawing and no neighbour

btsp_parameters.name: ec3_projection
btsp_parameters.why: fixed random positive weights in [0, 1) from EC to every CA1 cell decide which cells plateau: the m most driven (stand-in for the plateau threshold)

btsp_parameters.name: recall_readout
btsp_parameters.why: k-winners-take-all keeps the m most driven CA1 cells, ties broken at random (stand-in for feedback inhibition); m is the plateau count, no new value

btsp_parameters.name: return_rule
btsp_parameters.why: CA1-to-EC weights grow by CA1 activity times EC activity, from zero, no ceiling; its rate drops out of every cosine score
